title: Section-normalized evaluation of ordinary scalar extension
statement: Let J be an essentially small site with coefficient universe max(c,v,r), B,tau and D,sigma inverse ring-sheaf sequences, phi a ring-system morphism with section components alpha_n, S its ScalarData and M a B-system [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. For each n, morphisms from evaluation_n(S.model.E(M)) to a D_n-module N are naturally equivalent to morphisms from evaluation_n M to N with scalars restricted along alpha_n. The equivalences commute with postcomposition. If v is heterogeneously equal to a times scalarExtensionSection(phi,S,M,(n,U),x), then f(v) equals a times the corresponding restricted-linear morphism evaluated on x.

proof.text: Precompose a map out of the evaluated extension with the constructed isomorphism, then apply the ordinary sheafified tensor/restriction Hom equivalence. Its postcomposition equation is tensorHomEquiv_naturality_right. Its value on a root section is evaluation on the sheafified tensor 1 tensor x, which the preceding unit calculation identifies with the stated scalar-extension section. The evaluation functors retain the section carriers, giving the displayed formula directly on sections. Evaluation transports the scalar action along evaluation_ring; its component ring map is the identity. Thus a raw scalar multiple is the corresponding evaluated scalar multiple. Linearity of f upgrades the unit-generator equation to the formula for any scalar a, and heterogeneous equality allows any evaluated representative v.

theorem scalarExtension_evaluation
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (B D : ℕ → Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (τ : ∀ n, B (n + 1) ⟶ B n) (σ : ∀ n, D (n + 1) ⟶ D n)
    (α : ∀ n, B n ⟶ D n)
    (φ : systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ ⟶ systemRing.{c, v, max c v r} J D σ)
    (hφ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Cᵒᵖ), φ.hom.app (op (n, U.unop)) = (α n).hom.app U)
    (S : ScalarData.{c, v, max c v r} φ)
    (M : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ Ψ : ∀ N : Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J (D n),
      ((evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J D σ n).obj (S.model.E.obj M) ⟶ N) ≃
        ((evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ n).obj M ⟶ (res.{c, v, max c v r} (α n)).obj N),
      (∀ {N N'} (f : (evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J D σ n).obj (S.model.E.obj M) ⟶ N)
        (g : N ⟶ N'), Ψ N' (f ≫ g) = Ψ N f ≫ (res.{c, v, max c v r} (α n)).map g) ∧
      (∀ N (f : (evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J D σ n).obj (S.model.E.obj M) ⟶ N)
        (U : Cᵒᵖ) (a : (D n).obj.obj U) (x : M.val.obj (op (n, U.unop)))
        (v : ((evaluation.{c, v, max c v r} J D σ n).obj (S.model.E.obj M)).val.obj U),
        HEq v (a • scalarExtensionSection.{c, v, r} φ S M (op (n, U.unop)) x) →
        f.val.app U v = a • (show N.val.obj U from (Ψ N f).val.app U x))
